episodes.154936: A strong cold front moved through the area during the afternoon hours of Feb 15th.  The airmass ahead of the front was relatively unstable, and shear was very strong.  The result was a round of strong to severe storms across the tri-state area with damaging winds and a few tornadoes, including a strong EF2 tornado in Early county, GA.
episodes.155176: A squall line that formed ahead of a strong cold front pushes through the Gulf of Mexico bringing strong marine wind gust.
episodes.155303: A warm front shifted north through the area in advance of a low pressure system and associated cold front tracking across the Deep South, leading to deep moisture, instability and sufficient forcing for strong to severe thunderstorms across southeast Georgia.
episodes.155304: A warm front shifted north through the area in advance of a low pressure system and associated cold front tracking across the Deep South, leading to deep moisture, instability and sufficient forcing for strong to severe thunderstorms across southeast South Carolina.
episodes.155305: A warm front shifted north through the area in advance of a low pressure system and associated cold front tracking across the Deep South, leading to deep moisture, instability and sufficient forcing for strong to severe thunderstorms across marine waters off the southeast South Carolina coast.
episodes.155335: Veering southerly flow ahead of an approaching cold front helped to advect a rich plume of low-level moisture across South Florida. As showers and thunderstorms associated with the front pushed through the area and stalled, this translated into heavy rainfall and flooding across east coast metro. Also, lightning strikes from one storm struck and damaged the Broward Water Treatment Plant.
episodes.155336: Veering southerly flow ahead of an approaching cold front helped to advect a rich plume of low-level moisture across South Florida. As showers and thunderstorms associated with the front pushed through the area and stalled, this translated into heavy rainfall and flooding across east coast metro. A few of these storms produced strong wind gusts across the Atlantic waters as they moved offshore.
episodes.155452: A cluster of thunderstorms moved northeast across north Merritt Island and the barrier island north of Cape Canaveral, then moved offshore. Strong wind gusts accompanied the storms as they moved across the Cape area.
episodes.155453: A line of showers and thunderstorms associated with a cold front produced strong wind gusts along portions of the Indian River County coast.
episodes.156231: Isolated thunderstorm associated with a cold front produced a lightning strike which caused damage to a home across portions of southeast Virginia.
episodes.156264: Low pressure brought rain and wintry precipitation to the region February 15th into the 16th. A few instances of minor flooding were observed, but nothing too widespread.
episodes.156532: Strong low pressure and a cold front produced an EF-3 tornado.

The tornado touched down near the intersection of Old Georgetown Road SW and Angel Trace Road as an EF-0, where a couple of pine trees were snapped and several large limbs were broken. It moved to the northeast across a forest, then rapidly intensified to an EF-2 as it approached Hwy 904. A large portion of a roof was blown off a metal building on the west side of 904, several RVs were rolled over, and several large pine trees were snapped. The tornado crossed Hwy 904, snapped numerous trees and caused moderate damage to a large metal building and church.||The tornado entered the Ocean Ridge Plantation neighborhood with wind speeds up to 125 mph. Hundreds of trees were snapped, and many homes sustained minor to moderate damage. It crossed Rosebury Court SW, then strengthened to its maximum intensity of 160 mph (EF-3), as it approached Cambria Court SW. Two homes were completely destroyed in this area, and several more sustained moderate to major damage. The tornado reached its maximum path width of 275 yards as it moved across Windsor Circle, although maximum winds decreased to 115 mph (EF2). Many homes sustained moderate to major damage, hundreds of large trees were snapped, and one automobile was observed rolled on its side.||It crossed Hwy 17 as an EF-1, then re-intensified to an EF-2, causing major damage to several homes and snapping hundreds of trees along Green Bay Road NW and Old Shallote Road NW. The tornado continued to produce a near continuous path of tree damage through forest and swamp land, across Hwy 130 and Highway 211, confirmed by helicopter overflight. The tornado lifted approximately three miles east of highway 211 after passing west of the Bear Pen Airstrip.

A few hundred trees were snapped or uprooted by a microburst west of|the Bear Pen Airstrip. This damage occurred near, but separate from|the path of the tornado that damaged the Ocean Ridge Plantation |neighborhood about 20 minutes earlier.

The stream gage on Accotink Creek at Strathmeade Springs, VA. rose above flood stage during the specified time, reaching a max flood stage of 252.10 feet at 1:15 AM EST. At 251.5 feet elevation, Woodburn Road is covered by approximately six inches of water at its lowest point. Portions of the Cross County Trail are also flooded. At an elevation of 252.5 feet, both Woodburn Road and Prosperity Avenue become flooded by at least six inches of water.
Lightning strike caused damage to a home along Sunbeam Road.

A Weatherflow mesonet site along the coast at Indian River Shores recorded a peak wind gust of 38 knots from the northwest as line of showers and thunderstorms crossed the barrier island and continued to the Atlantic.

Several videos obtained from the media and public showed flash flooding on NE 23rd Street near Biscayne Blvd with water rising above the bottom line of several building doors, water covering the wheels of cars, and rising to knee-high level. Additional videos show street flooding near Margaret Pace Pack with an estimated two to three inches of water on the ground. Nearby rain gauges measured between 3 to 4 inches of rain in the area.

Lightning struck the Broward County 2A Water Treatment Plant located on Copans Road in Pompano Beach. The lightning damaged a number of mechanical, electrical, and instrumentation components including a high service pump, the control modules for two electronically actuated valves, and two programable logic controllers. The failure of this combination of items impeded their ability to fully pressurize the potable water distribution system, resulting in a precautionary boil water order to portions of Broward County.
